claim_text: 來源機構：Psychology and Education: A Multidisciplinary Journal (Innovative Scholars and Researchers Alliance)；資料標題：AI in the Teaching of Filipino: A Case Study of Teachers at Olutanga National High School；來源刊登日：2026-10-11。作者摘要報告：質性個案研究以 TPACK 為框架，探討菲律賓 Olutanga 國立中學 5 名菲律賓語科教師使用 AI 教學的經驗；作者報告教師主要以 ChatGPT、Grammarly、QuillBot、Canva AI 等工具備課、輔助寫作與製作視覺教材，並指出教師最需要的支持是持續且符合情境的培訓、明確的倫理指引與改善技術基礎設施，研究當時這些支持大多仍不足。（AI 輔助摘要，未經真人逐則審稿；請參閱原文。）
source_title: AI in the Teaching of Filipino: A Case Study of Teachers at Olutanga National High School
source_organization: Psychology and Education: A Multidisciplinary Journal (Innovative Scholars and Researchers Alliance)
source_locator: 首發日依 Crossref published-online（出版者頁與 PDF 只標年份，無上線日）：2026-10-11；出版者文章頁 https://scimatic.org/show_manuscript/11054 與出版者 PDF（HTTP 200）：Psych Educ Multidisc J 64(2): 146-157，Manuscript Accepted 09-05-2026；摘要歸屬：Abstract 第 2、3、5、8 句
original_excerpt: This study investigated the experiences of Filipino teachers at Olutanga National High School in using AI in their teaching, guided by the TPACK framework. … Using a qualitative case study design, five Filipino teachers with direct experience using AI were purposively selected. … Findings showed that teachers used AI tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, and Canva AI primarily for lesson preparation, writing support, and visual materials development. … Teachers identified continuous and context-specific training, clear ethical guidelines, and improved technical infrastructure as the support most needed for the responsible use of AI, support that remained largely inadequate at the time of the study.
interpretation_note: 轉述作者摘要的研究設計、對象、教師使用 AI 的工具與用途，以及教師認為最需要的支持；質性描述研究，非介入研究。

summary_evidence_spans: This study investigated the experiences of Filipino teachers at Olutanga National High School in using AI in their teaching, guided by the TPACK framework.
Using a qualitative case study design, five Filipino teachers with direct experience using AI were purposively selected.
Findings showed that teachers used AI tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, and Canva AI primarily for lesson preparation, writing support, and visual materials development.

Teachers identified continuous and context-specific training, clear ethical guidelines, and improved technical infrastructure as the support most needed for the responsible use of AI, support that remained largely inadequate at the time of the study.
